anomalies.observed: The two MCU footprint variants are wired to different nets on the same physical pins. U3 (THT) correctly maps PB3/XTAL1 to pin 2 = NET0004 and PB4/XTAL2 to pin 3 = NET0003. U4 (SMD) instead labels PB3 as pin 4 carrying NET0004 (while pin 4 is also GND on the left side, so NET0004 is shorted to GND and pin 2 is missing entirely), and labels PB4/pin 3 as NET0005 rather than NET0003.
anomalies.expected: U3 and U4 are alternative THT/SMD footprints for the same controller (marked 'THT' and 'SMD' beside the parts) and must therefore be pin-compatible: PB3 must be pin 2 on both, PB4 must be pin 3 on both, and pin 4 must be GND on both, with the same net on each pin.

evidence.quote: U4 ATtiny13V-10S right side: 'PB3 4' -> NET0004, 'PB4 3' -> NET0005; left side 'GND 4' (sheet fan_controller.kicad_sch, right tile)
U3 ATtiny45-20P right side: 'XTAL1/PB3 2' -> NET0004, 'XTAL2/PB4 3' -> NET0003 (sheet fan_controller.kicad_sch, right tile)
J4 POT pin 2 = NET0004; J3 FAN pin 4 = NET0005; R1/D2 node = NET0003 (sheet fan_controller.kicad_sch, left tile)

anomalies.impact: On the SMD build the pot wiper (NET0004) is shorted to GND, so speed control is dead and the analog input is loaded to ground; the fan-PWM/collector net (NET0005) lands on PB4 instead of the Q1 base drive (NET0003), which is left unconnected to the MCU, so Q1 is not driven. The two variants are not interchangeable and the SMD assembly behaves completely differently from the intended (THT) design.

anomalies.observed: U2 is an LM1117-5.0 linear regulator, but both its input (VI, pin 1) and its output (VO, pin 2) are tied to the same +5V net; the separate VCC rail is not connected to the regulator input.
anomalies.expected: A 5.0 V regulator's input must be the unregulated supply (the VCC rail used for the fan/PMOS) so it can produce the +5V MCU rail; tying VI to VO bypasses the regulator and leaves VCC unregulated.

evidence.quote: U2 LM1117-5.0: pin 1 VI -> +5V, pin 2 VO -> +5V, pin 3 GND (sheet fan_controller.kicad_sch, right tile)
VCC appears as a distinct rail on R5, C2, JP2 and the Q2 PMOS source, separate from +5V (sheet fan_controller.kicad_sch, left tile)

anomalies.impact: The regulator performs no function; if +5V was meant to be derived from VCC, the MCU rail is not generated by the regulator and the VCC-to-+5V regulation path is broken.

parsed.summary: The schematic contains a real deviation: the SMD MCU footprint (U4) is wired to different nets than the THT footprint (U3) on the same pins, shorting the pot wiper (NET0004) to GND and misrouting the fan/PWM signals, so the two 'compatible' footprints are not interchangeable; the LM1117-5.0 regulator also has its input tied to its own output rail.
